audits.title: An audit of waiting times in the outpatient clinic in Inverness Sector A NHS Highland during the COVID-19 pandemic
audits.standard: First appointment within 12 weeks of referral
audits.setting: CMHT Inverness Sector A outpatient service, NHS Highland

cycle1.result: 140 (87.5%) given an appointment; mean wait 12 weeks for 103 (64%); 57 (36%) waited longer than 13 weeks; 20 (12.5%) referrals inadequate.

audits.other_findings: Delays due to DNAs, cancellations and postponement awaiting information. Plans to flag the 12-week deadline in a database and improve referral information.
audits.citation: Zinchenko O, Hyland J. An audit of waiting times in the outpatient clinic in Inverness Sector A NHS Highland during the COVID-19 pandemic. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S113-S113. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.331.

audits.title: Timely Care: An Audit of Time to Consultation for Patients Rweferred to Older Peoples Service CMHT North Leeds
audits.standard: LYPFT guidance: seen within 15 working days of referral (trust standard 80%); electronic documentation within 24 hours; GP letter within 2 weeks
audits.setting: Older People's Service CMHT, North Leeds, LYPFT

cycle1.result: 70% seen within 15 working days; reason for delay documented 33%; electronic documentation 100%, within 24 hours 73%; GP letter sent 87%, within 2 weeks 33%.

audits.intervention: Resident doctors added to gatekeeping assessment rota; reminders to document reasons for delay; record of patients not accepted with admin reminders to complete GP letters within 2 weeks

cycle2.result: 87% seen within 15 working days; reason for delay documented 40%; electronic documentation 97%, within 24 hours 61%; GP letter sent 79%, within 2 weeks 41%.

audits.other_findings: Referrals rose from 80 to 100. Documentation timeliness gave mixed results under greater service pressure.
audits.citation: Palmer C. Timely Care: An Audit of Time to Consultation for Patients Rweferred to Older Peoples Service CMHT North Leeds. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S335-S335. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11821.

audits.title: An audit of waiting times in a haematology clinic before and after the introduction of point-of-care testing.
audits.standard: Patient-set maximum clinic waiting time of 30 min (longer-term target 20 min)
audits.setting: Haematology clinic, Bishop Auckland General Hospital

cycle1.result: Patient survey of 50 consecutive patients set the standard; air-tube sample transport with electronic results did not achieve it despite repeated audits.

audits.intervention: Point-of-care testing in the clinic, with the backup analyser moved weekly and tests done by trained nurse specialists.

cycle2.result: Clinic waiting times consistently achieved the standard.

audits.other_findings: No numbers given in the abstract.
audits.citation: Galloway MJ, Woods RS, Nicholson SL, Foggin JJ, Elliott L. An audit of waiting times in a haematology clinic before and after the introduction of point-of-care testing. Clin Lab Haematol. 1999;21(3):201-205. doi:10.1046/j.1365-2257.1999.00218.x. PMID: 10448602.

audits.title: Using Lean Six Sigma techniques to improve efficiency in outpatient ophthalmology clinics.
audits.setting: Publicly funded tertiary referral outpatient ophthalmology clinic (Royal North Shore Hospital), New South Wales

cycle1.result: 19.4 patients per 240-minute session; median in-clinic time 131 minutes (IQR 133, 84-217 minutes).

audits.intervention: Lean Six Sigma: clinic schedule amendments, dedicated postoperative clinics and clear documentation templates.

cycle2.result: Patients per session increased 9% to 21.1 (p = 0.016); significant reduction in in-clinic duration.

audits.citation: Kam AW, Collins S, Park T, Mihail M, Stanaway FF, Lewis NL, et al.. Using Lean Six Sigma techniques to improve efficiency in outpatient ophthalmology clinics. BMC Health Serv Res. 2021;21(1):38. doi:10.1186/s12913-020-06034-3. PMID: 33413381.

audits.title: An audit of waiting times in the diabetic outpatient clinic: role of patients' punctuality and level of medical staffing.
audits.standard: Being seen within 30 minutes of appointment time
audits.setting: Diabetes outpatient follow-up clinics, Royal Infirmary, Edinburgh

cycle1.result: 18.8% seen by the doctor and 86% by the nurse within 30 minutes of appointment time.

audits.intervention: Strict adherence to appointment times (no effect), then combined with more doctors, lowering the patient:doctor ratio from 11.1:1 to 7.7:1.

cycle2.result: With both changes, 31% were seen by the doctor and 100% by the nurse within 30 minutes.

audits.other_findings: Strict appointment times alone gave 20% (doctor) and 82.2% (nurse); medical staffing was the key factor.
audits.citation: Perros P, Frier BM. An audit of waiting times in the diabetic outpatient clinic: role of patients' punctuality and level of medical staffing. Diabet Med. 1996;13(7):669-673. doi:10.1002/(sici)1096-9136(199607)13:7<669::aid-dia135>3.0.co;2-k. PMID: 8840103.
